headline: Penguins’ Bryan Rust out at least six weeks with lower-body injury
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Pittsburgh's Bryan Rust will miss at least six weeks with a lower-body injury, suffered when he collided hard into the boards during Monday's 5-4 loss to the Mammoth.

The timing hurts a forward who has been scoring at a high clip. Rust has three goals in seven games so far this season, but his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances) sit at 1.55, so he has been running about 1.45 goals above what those chances would normally yield. Some of that output is likely to cool. Even so, he has been useful to the team: the Penguins' share of expected goals is 13.37 percentage points better when he is on the ice. Pittsburgh is 3-6-1 and already short on margin, though its 53 percent share of expected goals at five-on-five suggests the underlying play is better than the record. Losing a player who drives that play stings regardless of his shooting luck.

Going by how the coach has used his players, Ben Kindel (16:41 a night) is next in line for Rust's minutes. Rust has not yet missed a game, so this is a projection, not a record of games played without him.
